title: Quasi Coherent and Coherent Sheaves and Vector Bundles

items.title: Module sheaf on an affine scheme
items.statement: For an A-module M, assign M_f to every distinguished open D(f) of Spec A, with the canonical localization restriction maps; write tilde M for the resulting O-module after the sheaf construction. The zero ring and empty spectrum are included.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.title: Associated module sheaf exists
items.statement: Assume AC. The distinguished-open data for any A-module M form a sheaf on the basis and extend uniquely to an O_Spec A-module tilde M; its sections on D(f) are M_f, including D(0)=empty.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: Use AC only through compactness/prime existence for a finite distinguished refinement of a cover. For a finite cover of D(f), its elements generate the unit ideal in A_f. Clear finitely many denominators and use a finite unit-ideal relation to prove the localization Cech equalizer 0→M_f→product M_fgi ⇒ product M_fgigj. Extend the basis sheaf by locally representable germ families; verify the O action and uniqueness.

items.title: Quasi-coherent ideal sheaves
items.statement:
An ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ on $X$ is **quasi-coherent** if, for every affine
open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, there is an ideal $I\subseteq A$ such that
$\mathcal I|_U$ is the ideal sheaf associated to the $A$-module $I$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, Section 7

items.title: Stalk of an associated module sheaf
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited from existence. For p in Spec A, the canonical stalk map (tilde M)_p → M_p is an A_p-linear isomorphism, natural in M.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: A germ at p has a representative on some D(f) with f outside p. The filtered colimit of M_f over these f is M_p; verify both directions using the fraction equality criterion.

items.title: Sections of an associated sheaf on a basic open
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited from sheaf existence. Gamma(D(f),tilde M)=M_f naturally in M and f, and restrictions correspond to further localization.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: The extension from the distinguished-open basis recovers the original module on each basis open; check equality for D(f)=D(g) and commutation of restriction squares.

items.title: An associated sheaf restricts to an associated sheaf on any affine open
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited from the associated-sheaf construction. Let W=Spec C be any affine open subscheme of Spec A and let M be an A-module. The inclusion induces A→C and a canonical isomorphism (tilde M)|W ≅ tilde(C⊗_A M) as O_W-modules; W need not be distinguished in Spec A.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: Restrict each global section m of tilde M to W and use the C-action to obtain C⊗_A M→Γ(W,(tilde M)|W). For each distinguished D_W(c), localize this map to (C⊗_A M)_c and send its fractions to the restrictions of sections on W, multiplying by c^(-1) on D_W(c). These maps commute with further restriction, so the basis-sheaf construction gives a canonical sheaf map tilde(C⊗_A M)→(tilde M)|W. At q∈W corresponding to p∈Spec A, the open-subscheme definition identifies C_q=O_W,q with O_Spec A,p=A_p. The map on stalks is C_q⊗_A M→M_p, an isomorphism by localization. Stalkwise isomorphism proves the claim without any quasi-coherence or pullback theorem.

items.title: Quasi-coherent module on a scheme
items.statement: An O_X-module F is quasi-coherent if every point has an affine open neighbourhood U=Spec A for which F|U is isomorphic to tilde M for an A-module M.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.title: Descent of modules on a finite principal cover
items.statement: For a finite principal cover Spec A=union D(f_i) and A_fi-modules M_i with A_fifj-linear overlap isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle, the equalizer M of product M_i ⇒ product M_ij satisfies M_fi≅M_i compatibly.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: Define M by compatible tuples. Localization is exact and commutes with finite products. After localizing at f_i, the cover contains D(f_i) itself, so the equalizer reduces to M_i using the cocycle; no arbitrary-index choice is used.

items.title: Affine quasi-coherent sheaves are modules
items.statement: Assume AC as used to construct associated sheaves and finite principal refinements. For X=Spec A, M↦tilde M and F↦Gamma(X,F) are quasi-inverse equivalences Mod_A≃QCoh(X), including morphisms and the zero ring.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: The unit is Γ(Spec A,tilde M)=M. For QC F on Spec A, each point has an affine chart V where F=tilde N. Choose an A-distinguished neighbourhood D(f) inside V; the affine-open restriction lemma makes F|D(f) associated even when D(f) is not distinguished in V. Quasi-compactness yields finitely many such D(f). Their overlap module maps satisfy the cocycle; apply principal module descent and glue the local sheaf isomorphisms. The resulting M is Γ(Spec A,F). Full faithfulness follows by checking that maps on D(f) are localizations of their global A-linear map. AC is inherited from associated-sheaf existence and finite refinement.

items.title: Affine quasi-coherent sheaf determined by sections
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. Every QC F on Spec A is canonically isomorphic to tilde Gamma(Spec A,F); a map of QC sheaves is determined uniquely by its global A-module map.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: Apply the counit and full faithfulness of the affine equivalence; naturality gives the canonical identification.

items.title: Checking quasi-coherence on an affine cover
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. An O_X-module is quasi-coherent iff its restriction to every member of one affine open cover is associated to a module; then it is associated on every affine open of X, with canonical restriction compatibility.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: For every affine U=Spec A and x∈U choose a member V of the given affine cover containing x. An A-distinguished D(f) lies inside U∩V around x; the affine-open restriction lemma makes F|D(f) associated, since D(f) is affine open in V. Choose finitely many D(f) covering U, then apply principal descent and affine equivalence to identify F|U with tilde Γ(U,F); restrictions are canonical. The reverse direction follows from the local definition. No simultaneous principality in two affine charts is assumed.

items.title: Kernels and cokernels of quasi-coherent modules
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. On every scheme, kernels, images and cokernels of maps of quasi-coherent O_X-modules are quasi-coherent; QCoh(X) is an abelian full subcategory of O_X-modules. No quasi-separatedness is required.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: On each affine chart identify the map with M→N. Localization is exact, so the associated sheaves of kernel, image and cokernel match sheaf kernel, image and cokernel on all stalks. Glue by locality; finite sums and the zero sheaf are similarly associated.

items.title: Tensor product preserves quasi-coherence
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. If F,G are quasi-coherent on any scheme X, then F tensor_OX G is quasi-coherent and on Spec A equals tilde(M tensor_A N).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: Check on affine charts and stalks: (M tensor N)_p≅M_p tensor_Ap N_p. The canonical morphism between associated sheaf and sheaf tensor product is a stalkwise isomorphism.

items.title: Scheme pullback preserves quasi-coherence
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. For any scheme morphism f:X→Y and quasi-coherent F on Y, f*F is quasi-coherent; on affine U=Spec B mapping into V=Spec A with F|V=tilde M it is tilde(B tensor_A M).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: Cover X by affine U mapping into affine V. Compute the stalks of O_X tensor_f^-1 O_Y f^-1 F as B_q tensor_A M and compare with tilde(B tensor_A M); these agree on charts and restrictions.

items.title: Quasi-coherence of pushforward for qcqs morphisms
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. If f:X→S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then f_*F is quasi-coherent for every quasi-coherent O_X-module F.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: Work over an affine target. Choose finitely many affine U_i covering X and finite affine covers U_ijk of each overlap, using qc and qs respectively. For each affine source chart Spec B→Spec A, the anti-equivalence gives A→B; on every target D(a), its inverse image is D_B(a), so the direct-image sections of F are Γ(Spec B,F)_a. Thus each restricted affine pushforward is associated to its B-module, viewed over A. The sheaf equalizer 0→f_*F→finite sum f_i*F_i→finite sum f_ijk*F_ijk identifies f_*F as the kernel of QC sheaves; no higher cohomology is invoked.

items.title: Finite type and finite presentation module sheaves
items.statement: A quasi-coherent O_X-module is finite type if locally there is a surjection O^n→F; it is finitely presented if locally O^m→O^n→F→0 is exact for finite m,n. On sufficiently small affine charts these are finite and finitely presented modules respectively.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.title: Coherent sheaf on a scheme
items.statement: A quasi-coherent O_X-module F is coherent if it is finite type and for every open U and every morphism O_U^n→F|U with n finite, the kernel is finite type locally. On locally Noetherian schemes the later theorem identifies this with finite type.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.title: Coherent sheaves on a locally Noetherian scheme
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited through the quasi-coherent interfaces. On a locally Noetherian scheme, coherent sheaves are exactly finite-type quasi-coherent sheaves; kernels, cokernels and extensions of coherent sheaves are coherent.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: On each Noetherian affine chart, finite modules are finitely presented and all submodules of finite modules are finite. Apply that to kernels/images and the finite-generation lifting in a short exact sequence; glue the local conclusions. AC is inherited from the prior QC equivalence, not a new arbitrary selection.

items.title: Internal Hom of quasi-coherent sheaves
items.statement: For O_X-modules F,G, internal Hom has sections over U equal to Hom_OU(F|U,G|U). If F is finitely presented quasi-coherent and G quasi-coherent, the next lemma proves this Hom is quasi-coherent; no such claim is made for arbitrary F.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.title: Internal Hom from a finitely presented sheaf is quasi-coherent
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. If F is finitely presented quasi-coherent and G is quasi-coherent, then sheaf Hom(F,G) is quasi-coherent; on an affine chart with F=tilde M and G=tilde N it is tilde Hom_A(M,N).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: Use a local finite free presentation of M; Hom is its kernel into finite sums of N. Localization is exact and commutes with finite sums, giving Hom_A(M,N)_f≅Hom_Af(M_f,N_f). Compare all basic-open sections and glue. Finite presentation is used exactly here.

items.title: Finite locally free sheaf and rank
items.statement: An O_X-module E is locally free of rank r≥0 near x if E|U≅O_U^r on an open neighbourhood; finite locally free means such a finite rank exists locally, possibly varying by connected component. Rank zero is the zero sheaf.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.title: Dual and base change for finite locally free sheaves
items.statement: For finite locally free E, E^vee=Hom(E,O_X) is finite locally free of the same rank, E→E^vee vee is an isomorphism, and f*(E^vee)≅(f*E)^vee for any scheme morphism f.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: On each trivializing chart E=O^r, the dual basis identifies Hom(E,O)=O^r and makes evaluation an isomorphism. Under a change-of-frame matrix T the dual transition is inverse transpose, so these local isomorphisms agree on overlaps. Pullback preserves these matrices and local bases; the construction and proof use no choice axiom.

items.title: Symmetric algebra of a quasi-coherent module
items.statement: For a quasi-coherent module F define Sym(F)=T(F)/(sections v⊗w−w⊗v), graded with degree zero O_X and degree one F; on Spec A with F=tilde M this is the associated sheaf of Sym_A(M).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Constructions of Schemes §27.6

items.title: Symmetric algebras are quasi-coherent and commute with pullback
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. For quasi-coherent F, Sym(F) is a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra, compatible with restriction and any scheme pullback: f*Sym(F)≅Sym(f*F), as graded algebras. For F=O^r it is O[T_1,...,T_r].

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Constructions of Schemes §27.6

items.strategy: On affine charts, localize the tensor algebra degree by degree. Localization commutes with the direct sum of all graded degrees, tensor powers, and the quotient by the commutativity relations. The same presentation commutes with extension of scalars because tensor product is a left adjoint. These degreewise identifications respect multiplication and glue; Sym(O^r)=O[T_1,...,T_r].

items.title: Geometric vector bundle with the sections convention
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited from relative Spec. A rank-finite geometric vector bundle over X is an affine X-scheme whose relative coordinate algebra has a grading and is Zariski locally the graded polynomial algebra Sym(O_U^r), with transition isomorphisms induced by invertible linear maps of degree one; r is locally constant and rank 0 is allowed. For finite locally free E on X define its geometric total space V(E)=Spec_X Sym(E^vee), locally A^r_X, with V(0)=X. Morphisms of geometric vector bundles preserve the graded linear structure.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Constructions of Schemes §27.6

items.title: Finite locally free sheaves and geometric vector bundles
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. E↦V(E)=Spec_X Sym(E^vee) is a covariant equivalence from finite locally free sheaves to rank-finite geometric vector bundles with linear morphisms; its inverse is the sheaf of sections. Equivalently F↦Spec_X Sym(F) is the contravariant coordinate-module convention, recovered from the degree-one coordinate part.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Constructions of Schemes §27.6

items.strategy: On each trivializing chart, a section is an r-tuple and a linear bundle map is an r-by-s matrix. The map E→F induces F^vee→E^vee and thus V(E)→V(F); dualizing the transition matrices shows the section sheaf is E. Conversely glue local affine-space charts from the transition matrices. With Sym(F) without the dual, relative Spec reverses arrows; distinguish the two conventions.

items.title: Invertible sheaf
items.statement: An invertible O_X-module is a locally free sheaf of rank exactly one.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.title: Dual of a line bundle is its tensor inverse
items.statement: For every invertible sheaf L, evaluation gives a canonical isomorphism L^vee tensor L ≅ O_X, and the inverse transition units are those of L^vee.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: On each rank-one frame e with dual e*, evaluation sends e*⊗e to 1; on overlaps the transition units cancel. These local isomorphisms glue. The argument is choice-free.

items.title: Support of a module sheaf
items.statement: For an O_X-module F, Supp(F)={x∈X:F_x≠0}; it is a set of stalks, not the set where a chosen global section is nonzero.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.title: Support of a finite-type quasi-coherent sheaf is closed
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. On any scheme, a finite-type quasi-coherent F has closed support; on affine U=Spec A with F=tilde M it equals V(Ann_A M).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: For a finite module on each affine chart apply the published support-annihilator formula. The affine closed subsets agree on overlaps because stalk support is intrinsic; their complements form an open cover of X. No Noetherian assumption is used.

items.title: Fibre of a module sheaf at a point
items.statement: For x∈X define F(x)=F_x tensor_{O_X,x} κ(x)=F_x/m_x F_x. This residue-field vector space differs from the stalk F_x, which remains an O_X,x-module.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.title: Geometric Nakayama for finite-type sheaves
items.statement: For a finite-type quasi-coherent F, F(x)=0 iff F vanishes on some neighbourhood of x. If finitely many local sections span F(x), then they generate F on some affine neighbourhood of x. This local argument uses the determinant trick and makes no new arbitrary-index choice.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: At the local ring, the cokernel Q of the proposed generators satisfies Q/mQ=0. The determinant trick yields (1-a)Q=0 for a∈m, and 1-a is a unit, hence Q=0. On a local affine chart Q is finite; choose finitely many generators, each killed by some element outside the prime, and multiply those elements to shrink to D(f) where Q=0. Empty generator list gives local vanishing.

items.title: Openness of the finite free locus
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finitely presented quasi-coherent F and r≥0, the locus where F_x is free of rank r is open, and on a neighbourhood of each such point F is isomorphic to O^r. Fibre dimension r alone is insufficient without the relation-kernel check.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: Near a point with free rank-r stalk, choose r local lifts of a basis and shrink until O^r→F is surjective by geometric Nakayama. Finite presentation makes its kernel finite type; the kernel stalk at x is zero, so shrink again until the kernel vanishes. For r=0 use the vanishing case directly.

items.title: Fitting minors do not depend on a presentation
items.statement: For a finite A-module M and integer k≥0, the ideal of (n−k)-minors of a relation matrix for any surjection A^n→M is independent of the finite generating surjection, even when the relation module is not finitely generated. Use I_r=A for r≤0 and I_r=0 for r larger than the number of available rows or columns. The ideal commutes with localization and base change.

references.title: The Stacks Project, More on Algebra §15.8
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: Replace an arbitrary relation generating family by all vectors of the kernel. For two finite surjections F→M and F′→M, lift the basis of F′ into F, compare both with F⊕F′→M, and conjugate by the elementary shear to the augmented presentation K⊕F′→F⊕F′. Laplace expansion on the identity block and determinantal containment show augmentation leaves I_{n-k} unchanged; repeat symmetrically. Localizing or tensoring a presentation preserves its cokernel, and minors commute with coefficient maps. No Schanuel lemma is silently imported.

items.title: Fitting ideal sheaf
items.statement: Assume AC. For finite-type quasi-coherent F and k≥0, define Fitt_k(F) affine locally from (n−k)-minors of a presentation A^(J)→A^n→M→0, using I_r=A for r≤0 and I_r=0 when r exceeds the available rows or columns; set Fitt_{−1}(F)=0 separately. Presentation independence and localization compatibility make these quasi-coherent ideal sheaves.

references.title: The Stacks Project, More on Algebra §15.8
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.title: Fitting ideals control fibre generator loci
items.statement: Assume AC. For finite-type quasi-coherent F, V(Fitt_r(F))={x:dim_{κ(x)}F(x)>r} and D(Fitt_r(F))={x:dim F(x)≤r}; Fitt_0 cuts out Supp(F). If F is finite locally free of rank r then Fitt_{r−1}=0 and Fitt_r=O. Conversely these equalities on an open imply F is free rank r there. Mere pointwise fibre rank r need not imply local freeness.

references.title: The Stacks Project, More on Algebra §15.8
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: Reduce a presentation matrix over κ(x): fibre dimension is n−rank(matrix). The relevant minors vanish precisely when rank<n−r. The free case has zero relation matrix after r generators; conversely Fitt_r=O permits r local generators, and Fitt_{r−1}=0 kills every relation entry in such a presentation. Include r=0 and note that V(Fitt_{r−1})∩D(Fitt_r) only fixes fibre rank, not freeness.

items.title: Quasi-coherent ideals and closed subschemes, complete route
items.statement: Assume AC as used by the affine quotient supplier. For any scheme X, quasi-coherent ideal sheaves I⊂O_X correspond bijectively to closed subschemes Z↪X via I↦Spec_X(O_X/I) and Z↦ker(O_X→i_*O_Z), including the empty subscheme.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: On each affine U=Spec A, the ideal I|U is tilde J for a unique J⊂A by the affine QC equivalence. Glue Spec(A/J) across principal restrictions. Conversely use the batch-5 local affine-quotient proof for any closed immersion; kernels are tilde J and agree on overlaps. The two constructions invert chartwise. Do not use the published correspondence or its published affine-quotient theorem to prove this replacement; AC enters exactly through the batch-5 affine-quotient supplier.

items.title: Quasi-coherent ideals and closed subschemes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For a scheme $X$, the assignments
$\mathcal I\mapsto V(\mathcal I)$ and
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X\mapsto\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$
give mutually inverse correspondences between quasi-coherent ideal sheaves on
$X$ and closed subschemes of $X$.
items.strategy: Assume AC explicitly. Use the completed in-run affine quotient and quasi-coherent ideal correspondence suppliers, identify the quotient ringed subspace by stalks on affine charts, and verify both inverse assignments including the empty case.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 2.3

items.title: Scheme-theoretic image of a quasi-compact morphism
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes and put
$\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X)$. Then $\mathcal I$ is a
quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and the closed subscheme $V(\mathcal I)$ is the
scheme-theoretic image of $f$. For every open $W\subseteq Y$, its restriction
$V(\mathcal I)\cap W$ is the scheme-theoretic image of
$f^{-1}(W)\to W$.
items.strategy: Under AC, for a quasi-compact morphism define the image ideal as the kernel of O_Y to f_*O_X. On an affine target chart, take a finite affine cover of the inverse image; on each principal target open, restrict this cover to principal source opens and use exact localization of its finite-product kernel. This proves quasi-coherence and compatibility with restriction; then use the AC-dependent closed-subscheme correspondence and verify minimality chartwise. No quasi-separated hypothesis is required by Stacks Lemma 29.6.3.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.6.3

items.title: Finite type need not mean coherent
items.statement: Over a non-Noetherian ring, finite type and coherent are distinct: the relation-kernel condition must be checked. The locally Noetherian equivalence does not extend to arbitrary bases, and finite presentation alone does not assert coherence.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

title: Quasi Coherent and Coherent Sheaves and Vector Bundles — Examples

items.title: Quotient module sheaf and its support
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. For an ideal I⊂A, tilde(A/I)=O_Spec A/tilde I and its support is V(I), including I=A.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: On every D(f), (A/I)_f=A_f/I_f. At p this is nonzero exactly when I⊂p, so the support is V(I); sheaf quotient agrees by exact localization.

items.title: Restricting an associated sheaf to a localization
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. For f∈A and any A-module M, tilde(M_f) on Spec A_f corresponds under Spec A_f≅D(f) to tilde M restricted to D(f).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: For a basic open D(fg) inside D(f), compare (M_f)_g with M_fg and check restrictions, then glue the basis identifications.

items.title: A coherent closed-point skyscraper
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. For a Noetherian ring A and maximal ideal m, tilde(A/m) is coherent on Spec A, has stalk A/m at m and zero stalk elsewhere, and is the direct image of its one-point fibre.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: A/m is finite over Noetherian A. Its localization vanishes at primes not containing m, and maximality leaves only m; the remaining local module is the residue field.

items.title: Twists on the two-affine projective line
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. On P^1_k with charts Spec k[t], Spec k[u], u=t^(-1), the gluing relation e_infty=t^n e_0 defines O(n), an invertible sheaf for every integer n; dual and tensor have indices −n and n+m.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
Gao and Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry, projective-line gluing

items.strategy: Use the published two-affine twist definition. Transition is a unit in k[t,t^(-1)]; invert and multiply transition functions for dual and tensor. Check n=0 and the frame orientation.

items.title: Global sections do not determine a sheaf on P1
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. On P^1_k, the nonzero invertible sheaf O(−1) and the zero sheaf both have zero global sections, so the affine global-sections determination fails on this nonaffine scheme.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
Gao and Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry, projective-line gluing

items.strategy: A global section is a(t)e_0=b(u)e_infty with a∈k[t], b∈k[u], and e_infty=t^(−1)e_0. Hence a(t)=t^(−1)b(t^(−1)) forces a=b=0. Each chart restriction of O(−1) is O, so the sheaf is nonzero.

items.title: Quasi-separatedness in pushforward cannot be omitted
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. There is a quasi-compact non-quasi-separated f:X→Spec A with f_*O_X not quasi-coherent: take A=k[t,z,x_1,x_2,...]/(t^i x_i^i z:i≥1), glue two copies of Spec A along U=union_i D(x_i), and let f be the evident map.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Examples §110.30

items.strategy: U is not quasi-compact: the point with only x_i nonzero witnesses failure of any finite subcover. The monomial-ideal test shows A→product A_xi injective: for a finite polynomial choose n outside its variable support with n larger than all t-degrees, so x_n cannot annihilate a surviving monomial. Thus Gamma(X,O)=A diagonally. In A_t, z survives since no defining monomial divides t^m z, but z dies in every A_tx_i. Therefore (z,0) is a section over f^(-1)D(t) not in A_t, contradicting affine QC localization.

items.title: Finite type need not be locally free
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. On Spec k[x], the finite-type coherent sheaf tilde(k[x]/(x)) is not locally free: its fibre dimension is one at (x) and zero away from (x).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17
The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes §30.9
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: Compute localizations and tensor with residue fields; local constancy of fibre rank for a finite locally free sheaf rules out local freeness at the origin.

items.title: Fitting ideals of a diagonal two-by-two presentation
items.statement: For A=k[x,y] and M=coker(diag(x,y):A^2→A^2), Fitt_0(M)=(xy), Fitt_1(M)=(x,y), Fitt_2(M)=A. The fibre dimension is two at the origin, one on either punctured coordinate axis, and zero elsewhere.

references.title: The Stacks Project, More on Algebra §15.8
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, §§28.20, 28.26

items.strategy: Compute the two-by-two determinant and the one-by-one minors, then reduce the diagonal matrix over residue fields pointwise.

items.title: The rank-zero bundle
items.statement: The zero sheaf is finite locally free of rank zero on every scheme, and its total space V(0)=Spec_X Sym(0) is the identity X→X, with one zero vector in every fibre.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: On any open, 0=O^0. Sym(0)=O in degree zero, so relative Spec is X; the zero section is the identity.

items.title: Stalk and fibre are different
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited. For X=Spec k[t], F=O_X and p=(t), the stalk F_p=k[t]_(t) is a local ring while the fibre F(p)=k; reduction modulo (t) is surjective but not an isomorphism.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, §§26.5, 26.7, 26.24
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022, Chapters 6, 14, 17

items.strategy: Identify O_X,p with A_p and tensor with κ(p)=A_p/(t); t/1 is nonzero in the stalk but zero in the fibre.
